_port_note: Unlike the Traction gate this one keeps BOTH options — the player may say not yet, and the reminder re-arms on a five-day clock. The escalating body is the one piece of variant text already shipping in the game (phase_gate_system.gd rewrites its own body by decline count), so the port needed a schema for it rather than a workaround. §7.4’s shutter hold is a CONDITION LEAF now, not an early return in two places. PhaseGateSystem held the scene at _open_gate and again at _tick_reminder, and a third path (on_shutter_cleared) existed to undo the hold; one leaf replaces all three, and the "why didn’t this fire" panel can name it. CONDITION IS THE RATCHET, not a second copy of the gate's own thresholds. The card first carried `phase.current` plus the revenue/growth/brand leaves, which read as the same question and is not: PhaseGateSystem latches `phase_gate_ready` and `pending_next_phase` and never re-evaluates after (§2.3), so a card re-asking the thresholds would go quiet the moment the player's MRR dipped — with the door still open and no way to walk through it. Reading the ratchet means the card says exactly what the system decided.
_schema_addition: body may be an object: {by_seam, variants}. That is EVENT_POOL_DESIGN_v1 §5.7's variant text, delivered narrowly for the one card that already needs it rather than as a general facility nobody has asked for yet. A missing variant falls back to the lowest key.
